checklist.description: In src/surfaces/cli/dispatch.rs, classify only SystemAction::FetchEmailGoals as exempt from the direct-target rejection. Document that its required target identifies the connection authorized by development_requests::fetch_email_goals. Preserve the production guard and every unrelated command classification.

Extend tests/cli_target_root.rs to execute CARGO_BIN_EXE_refine with separate arguments and temporary paths containing spaces and apostrophes. Initialize a real temporary Git target and valid local connection without credentials; require the specific missing email/fastmail_jmap_token error, proving production dispatch reached the capability without contacting mail. Both new routing tests must fail against the current guard.

Add the compiled mismatched-target case using distinct temporary targets, a malformed secret index, and retained ledger sentinels. Require the application’s different-target error before secret parsing, fetch-lock creation, or ledger processing; assert unchanged fixture state. Retain compiled tests for rejected goal --target-root arguments and daemon-required product commands, plus unit coverage that unrelated targets remain classified as restricted.

Preserve the existing handler and email-processing implementation. Extend existing application tests through MailSource where coverage is missing: sender filtering, durable recording before remote acknowledgement, successful imports surviving per-record failures, returned goal_ids/errors/batch_limit, retry evidence, deterministic deduplication, and ordinary Backlog creation. Retain MIME, legacy migration, and historical-record tests. Verify the unchanged handler prints JSON including fetched_count before returning nonzero for per-record errors. Put substantial new intake tests in a cohesive child module.

Update docs/runbooks/development-request-email.md with separately quoted executable, runtime-root, and target-root values. Keep fetch-goals-from-email.json consistent with the same command, 25-message batches, ten-batch maximum, and immediate stop on command failure. Clarify the bounded one-shot exception in docs/intent/05-surfaces/02-cli.md; preserve the existing Skills intent and prohibition on fetching approving Goals, changing Review decisions, or sending replies.

From the pinned worktree, run cargo test --locked --lib surfaces::cli::tests -- --test-threads=1; cargo test --locked --lib application::development_requests::tests -- --test-threads=1; cargo test --locked --test cli_target_root -- --test-threads=1; cargo build --release --locked --bin refine; cargo fmt --all -- --check; and git diff --check. Parse-check the Skill JSON and review its batch/stop instructions. Report actual test counts, baseline failures, and candidate evidence through the ordinary workflow, using isolated fixtures and preserving all live mail, credentials, records, and Goals.

rounds.prompt:
Fix the production CLI dispatch conflict that prevents the standalone Fetch Goals from Email Skill from importing requests into the selected project's Backlog.

Observed failure:
The Skill prescribed this command, which was run from /home/buddy/projects/refine-next:
'/home/buddy/projects/refine/bin/refine' system fetch-email-goals --runtime-root '/home/buddy/projects/refine/run/8082' --target-root '/home/buddy/projects/refine-next'

It exited with code 1:
direct --target-root CLI dispatch is not supported in normal operation; use the daemon API for target state mutations instead (/home/buddy/projects/refine-next)

The failure occurs before email fetching and before a JSON result is produced. No Goals were imported or recovered by that invocation. A read-only check found 34 existing request.json records retained under /home/buddy/projects/refine/run/8082/self-development-email/requests.

Diagnosis:
src/surfaces/cli/dispatch.rs applies a generic #[cfg(not(test))] explicit_target_root_path rejection before dispatch. That helper includes SystemAction::FetchEmailGoals, whose target_root is required. The existing handler in src/surfaces/cli/dispatch/system.rs is therefore unreachable in normal operation. The unit test email_fetch_cli_requires_the_pinned_target_before_accessing_mail in src/surfaces/cli/tests/system/commands.rs bypasses the production guard through cfg(test), allowing this regression to escape detection.

Requested change:
Implement a narrowly scoped dispatch correction that restores the documented one-shot capability while preserving the restrictions on other commands and the email capability's existing authorization and retry behavior. Keep docs/runbooks/development-request-email.md and docs/runbooks/skills/fetch-goals-from-email.json consistent with the supported command.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The documented system fetch-email-goals command, with separately and safely quoted runtime-root and target-root arguments, reaches the email-fetch capability in a production build.
2. A mismatched configured target is rejected before secret or request-ledger access.
3. Sender filtering, MIME extraction, deterministic Goal IDs, duplicate prevention, remote acknowledgement, and durable retries remain intact.
4. Successful fetches return the documented JSON fields, including fetched_count, batch_limit, goal_ids, and errors. Per-record failures retain successful imports and retry evidence while returning a nonzero exit.
5. Regression coverage executes the compiled CLI with production dispatch checks enabled and would fail on the current bug. Cover both reaching the fetch capability for the intended target and rejecting a mismatched target without secret or ledger access. Existing restrictions on unrelated commands remain effective.
6. Fetching retains ordinary Backlog creation behavior without approving Goals, changing Review decisions, or sending replies. Preserve the Skill's 25-message batch limit, maximum ten batches, and stop-on-command-failure behavior.
7. Run the focused CLI and development-request checks plus appropriate compiled-binary regression validation. Use isolated fixtures; preserve the live mailbox, token, raw email source, request ledger, and existing Goals.

Deliver the scoped fix and validation evidence through the ordinary Goal/Round workflow.

skill.name: Quality
skill.prompt:
## Quality review

Independently review the finalized plans and candidate implementation. Select or add meaningful tests, correct defects when needed, and run the relevant checks. Report actual commands, results and findings. Refine verifies the exact candidate and supervises evaluation commands.

## Required behavior

Preserve the relevant Goal and docs/intent product behavior. Keep Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces coherent; shared capabilities authoritative; local state and evidence inspectable and recoverable; and affected surfaces semantically consistent.

## Review and verification

Judge the candidate against the Goal and only the relevant docs/intent pages. Use the smallest deterministic checks that cover the affected behavior, adding or adjusting behavior-focused tests only when evidence is missing. Scale integration and failure-path checks to actual risk. Test the governing invariant through the affected real entry paths and lifecycle boundaries. Look for cases that could disprove the implementation's assumptions, including relevant callers outside the changed files. Group findings with a common cause into one coherent recovery request. Report exact commands, results, and remaining uncertainty. Do not require unrelated tests, documentation, refactors, or cleanup; documentation is relevant only when product intent or an architectural contract changes.

## Acceptance checks

- The candidate satisfies the Goal and relevant docs/intent contracts, preserves the existing architecture and consistent behavior across affected surfaces, and passes focused deterministic regression checks.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
